name: <module>.BoostCurve
strings:
Parameterized boost-vs-RPM curve for forced-induction engines.

    Model: smooth ramp from 0 PSI at low RPM, reaching peak_psi at peak_rpm,
    then either holding flat or tapering to redline_psi. Used to multiply
    base engine torque in CalcEngine acceleration sim.

    Effective torque: engine_tq * (1 + psi_at(rpm) * torque_per_psi_pct/100)

    Defaults represent a moderate ~10 PSI turbo on a 5.3L LS-truck setup.

name: <module>.BoostCurve.psi_at
strings:
RPM-dependent boost PSI. Three regions:
          - rpm < spool: linear ramp 0 → 0.5 PSI (pre-spool/turbo lag)
          - spool ≤ rpm < peak: cubic ramp 0.5 → peak_psi (boost building)
          - rpm ≥ peak: linear interp peak_psi → redline_psi

name: <module>.BoostCurve.torque_mult
strings:
Multiplier to apply to NA torque to get boosted torque.
        torque_mult(rpm) = 1 + psi_at(rpm) * (pct_per_psi / 100)

name: <module>.TorqueCurve
strings:
Stores RPM-indexed HP/TQ pairs and provides interpolated lookups.

    Storage: sorted list of (rpm, hp, tq) tuples. RPM strictly increasing.
    Empty curve falls back to flat RWHP scalar mode.

name: <module>.TorqueCurve.hp_at
strings:
Linear interpolation between data points; clamps to endpoints.
        Boost multiplier applied if boost_curve set.

name: <module>.TorqueCurve.avg_hp
strings:
Average HP across an RPM range (trapezoidal). Useful for shift-lead
        math: predict acceleration during the shift interval RPM band.

name: <module>.TorqueCurve.from_csv
strings:
Parse a dyno CSV. Expected: 1-3 columns (RPM, HP[, TQ]) with header.
        Tolerant of common dyno formats. Returns TorqueCurve.

name: <module>.LogImporter
strings:
Reads a dyno log CSV and analyzes against calc predictions.

    Column-name matching is fuzzy (case-insensitive substring match) to
    handle the wide variation across VCM Scanner / EFILive / OBDLink / etc.
    Common aliases are listed below; first match wins.

name: <module>.LogImporter.from_csv
strings:
Parse a CSV file. Auto-detects header row + column mapping.
        Returns a LogImporter instance.

        progress_cb : optional callable(int 0-100) for UI feedback
        target_hz   : if set, downsample to this rate (10 Hz typical = 10× speedup
                      and no analytical loss for shift detection / slip averaging)

        Uses pandas if available (10-50× faster on large files), else falls back
        to csv module.

name: <module>.LogImporter.analyze
strings:
Extract measured shift points, stall RPM, WOT slip%, ATF temp range.
        Compares to predicted values from cfg.

        Returns dict with:
          shift_events:    list of {gear_from, gear_to, mph, rpm, tps}
          stall_peak_rpm:  highest engine RPM observed while v < 5 mph and TPS > 80%
          wot_slip_pct:    average slip % at TPS > 90%, by computing
                           (engine_rpm - wheel_coupled_rpm) / engine_rpm × 100
          temp_range:      (min, max) ATF temp °F
          n_samples:       row count
          warnings:        list of strings noting columns not detected
No gear column — can't detect shift events. VCM Scanner: enable PID 'Current Gear' (TCM).

name: <module>.DragSimulator
strings:
Newton-integration vehicle dynamics simulator.

    Forces:
      F_drive = engine_tq × ratio × final_drive × η / r_tire
      F_aero  = 0.5 × ρ × Cd×A × v²
      F_roll  = Crr × W
      a       = (F_drive − F_aero − F_roll) × g / W

    Launch: engine sits at stall_rpm × 0.7 until vehicle speed catches up to
    rigid-coupling RPM (models converter flash but not full slip dynamics).
    Shifts: 0.4s torque interruption per shift event.

name: <module>.DragSimulator._slip_for_gear
strings:
Return fractional slip (0.06 = 6%) for gear at WOT, locked-converter-
        unaware. Used to reduce effective drive torque at the wheels.

name: <module>.DragSimulator._shift_time_for
strings:
Dynamic shift time. Real GM shifts:
          - WOT in 1st-2nd:    0.50-0.65s (most torque to manage)
          - WOT in 3rd-4th:    0.40-0.50s
          - WOT in upper:      0.30-0.40s
          - Light throttle:    0.15-0.25s (any gear)

        Returns seconds. torque_load_frac is 0-1, where 1 = WOT at peak HP.

name: <module>.DragSimulator.simulate
strings: Run the simulation. Returns dict with traces and timing results.

name: <module>.CalcEngine
strings:
Pure shift point calculator. Takes a config dict, returns numpy-like
    nested-list tables. UI binds inputs to this; logic is testable in isolation.

name: <module>.CalcEngine.base_slope
strings: Lock/unlock base curve: (TPS/100)^factor with offset shift.

name: <module>.CalcEngine.upshift_slope
strings:
Upshift curve: base + (aggressive - base) * blend[col].
        Aggressive uses (1-(1-x)^(factor + upf/10)) to keep WOT shifts firm
        while preserving smooth part-throttle. Column-dependent blend prevents
        overly early mid-throttle shifts.

name: <module>.CalcEngine.downshift_slope
strings:
Downshift slope: x^(factor + 0.1 + (10-downf)/5).

        downf high (e.g. 10) → exp small → slope LARGE → downshift cell at
        HIGH MPH → kickdown triggers readily even at cruise speed (aggressive).

        downf low (e.g. 1) → exp large → slope SMALL → downshift cell at
        LOW MPH → engine must lug down before PCM drops a gear (lazy).

        Behavioral inverse of upshift firmness — high downf = snappy kickdown,
        low downf = hunt-free cruise.

name: <module>.CalcEngine.vss_calibration
strings:
Compute speedometer calibration values per BC's Update_VSS logic.
        Returns dict of label->value pairs (for display in Export dialog).
        - tire_rev_per_mile = 63360 / (tire * π)
        - trans_rev_per_mile = tire_rev × axle_ratio
        - Pulses/Mile = trans_rev × VSS_count (or VSS/axle for tailshaft pickup)

name: <module>.CalcEngine.calculate
strings:
Main entry point. cfg is a dict with all calibration parameters.
        Returns dict of 2D tables: up_shift, down_shift, tcc_lock, tcc_unlock,
        speed_summary (per-gear WOT references).

name: <module>.LockupConfigDialog.__init__

the Min/Accel/WOT gear gates set in the Torque Converter group.

Stall Lock Logic — force lock above 66% of stall RPM
(prevents excessive slip with high-stall converters)

Init Lock Logic — TCC must lock above the upshift into this gear
(matches BC's InitLock; aggressive but smooth)

4L60E: Allow WOT 4th Lockup
(GM disables stock — enable for street tuning, NOT towing)

6L80/90: Disable 2nd Gear Coast-Down TCC
(reduces cruise lockup hunting)

  • Sports car (Vette, GT):       6-8

  • Performance street:     0.011-0.013
  • All-season:             0.013-0.015
  • Truck A/T or M/T tires: 0.015-0.020

  • All-season:           0.75-0.85

  • 8/10-spd:     0.86-0.88 (modern design)

name: <module>.PressureEngine
strings:
Pure-logic generator for Base Shift Pressure tables.
    Output: 2D list [temp_idx][torque_idx] → PSI.

    Model:
      1. Hot-side base curve: psi(tq) = base + (peak - base) * (tq/tq_max)^curve
      2. Cold preload (additive, saturates with torque):
         cold_factor = max(0, (68 - temp) / 90)        # 1.0 at -22°F, 0 at 68°F
         cold_add    = cold_preload * cold_factor * (1 - 0.82 * t_norm)
      3. Hot-side temp comp (intent-scaled, only > 68°F):
         hot_dev_pct = clamp((temp-68)/(257-68), 0, 1) * 0.18
         hot_mult    = 1 + hot_dev_pct * hot_scale
      4. Per-shift multiplier on base+peak
      5. Cap at MAX_PRESSURE_PSI (296 stock; raise if user has lifted Max Pressure)

name: <module>.PressureEngine.torque_cols
strings: 5 torque breakpoints, 0/25/50/75/100% of trans rated torque (lb·ft).

name: <module>.PressureEngine.base_shift_pressure
strings:
Generate one Base Shift Pressure table for the given intent/shift.

        intent_name: key into PRESSURE_INTENTS
        max_torque:  trans torque rating (lb·ft)
        shift_name:  e.g. "1-2", "1-3", "5-6"
        max_pressure_psi: hard ceiling (defaults to MAX_PRESSURE_PSI=296)
        Returns: 2D list [temp_idx][torque_idx] → PSI.

name: <module>.PressureEngine.tcc_apply_pressure
strings:
Generate TCC Apply Pressure table (Gen IV+ converter clutch).

        Same 5×5 axis as Base Shift Pressure (temp × torque) but uses TCC-
        specific intent profiles and a lower default cap (200 PSI). The
        converter clutch only needs to overcome slip torque, not full clutch
        pack capacity, so apply pressure runs ~30-180 PSI vs line pressure
        which runs ~95-296 PSI.

        Model is identical to base_shift_pressure() — same cold-preload
        lookup, same hot_scale formula — just different intent values and
        cap. No shift_mult since apply pressure is not per-shift.

name: <module>.PressureEngine.tcc_apply_pressure_ramp
strings:
Generate the TCC Apply Pressure Ramp table per HP Tuners layout.

        Stock GM control strategy by era:
        - 07-14: Smooth-ramp with spike at very negative slip (relief).
                 Pattern: tq<0 row low spike (~17 PSI), 0-90 tq HIGH spike
                 (148 PSI cap), 110+ tq moderate (~60 PSI). Cap 148 PSI.
        - 15+:   RPM-correlated correction deltas (8L90/8L45 EC3SS strategy).
                 0-50 PSI range, scales with engine RPM both directions.

        Returns 2D list [n_rows][n_cols] of PSI values.

name: <module>.PressureEngine._tcc_ramp_07_14
strings:
07-14 era: spike at very negative slip (TCC release), smooth ramp.
        Spike pattern (verified vs stock screenshot):
          tq < 0:        engine brake row stays relatively flat (15-18 PSI)
                         across the negative-spike zone
          0 ≤ tq < 100:  HIGH spike at -30 (148 PSI cap), drops rapidly to
                         ~30 at -25, ~20 at -20, ~3 at -17
          tq ≥ 110:      moderate (~60 PSI) at -30, slight non-monotonic
                         variation in -25/-20 cells
        Slip in [-15, -2] → very low band (~1-5 PSI)
        Slip = 0 → minimum (~0.15)
        Slip > 0 → mild ramp scaled by torque

name: <module>.PressureEngine._tcc_ramp_15_plus
strings:
2015+ era: RPM-correlated correction values, 0-50 PSI range.
        Both negative and positive slip scale with engine RPM.

name: <module>.PressureEngine._tcc_ramp_shudder_fix
strings:
Shudder Fix preset: maintains a constant plateau across ALL
        positive slip cells, preventing the slip-stick harmonic that
        causes TCC shudder. Common fix for 6L80 Gen-1 / worn converters.

        Plateau height scales with intent_max_psi so Shudder Fix Levels
        produce progressively firmer lockup:
          Mild       (max_psi=148) → ~65 PSI plateau (light fix)
          Moderate   (max_psi=165) → ~85 PSI plateau (mid-grade)
          Aggressive (max_psi=195) → ~110 PSI plateau (full lock)

        Pattern:
          slip < 0:  small relief (decay toward 0 as slip → 0)
          slip ≥ 0:  PLATEAU at intent-scaled PSI
          slip > 60: torque-scaled ramp on top of plateau

        Cap respected (148 stock 07-14, 200 newer trans).

name: <module>.PressureEngine.coast_pressure
strings:
Generate Coast-Down Pressure table for deceleration / lift-off.

        Same 5×5 axis as Base Shift Pressure (temp × torque). Different intent
        values: coast pressure is typically 60-75% of accel pressure since
        engine braking torque is much lower than drive torque. Towing intent
        actually runs HIGHER than its accel pressure to control decel under
        heavy load (engine brake reliance).

        Same cold-preload + hot-scale math as base_shift_pressure. Cap at
        MAX_COAST_PRESSURE_PSI (250 PSI default).

name: <module>.PressureEngine.garage_shift_pressure
strings:
Generate Garage Shift Pressure tables.

        Returns a dict keyed by direction (PD/PR/ND/NR), each value is a
        list of 5 PSI values (one per ATF temp). No torque axis — engagement
        always happens at idle torque, so single value per direction per temp.
        Cold ATF needs more pressure (sluggish valves); hot ATF needs less
        (thinner fluid grabs less, also cooler-protection mindset).

name: <module>.PressureEngine.base_shift_pressure_4spd
strings:
Generate 4-spd Base Shift Pressure table.
        Returns: 2D list [3 shifts][33 torque cols] -> PSI.
        Axes: rows = ["1-2","2-3","3-4"]; cols = PRESSURE_4SPD_TORQUE_COLS.
        4-spd uses a single torque-axis table per mode (no ATF temp axis).

name: <module>.PressureEngine.brake_shift_pressure_4spd
strings:
Generate 4-spd Brake Shift Pressure table (3 shifts × 32 torque cols).

        Shape per shift: starts at base_high (e.g. 90 PSI) at 0 torque, dips
        to valley_psi around valley_center torque, then ramps to high_end_psi
        at max torque. Reflects PCM strategy of relieving pressure for
        normal driving, then clamping firmly under heavy load or aggressive
        downshifts.

name: <module>.PressureEngine.force_motor_current
strings:
Generate Force Motor Current table (17 ATF temp rows × 18 PSI cols).
        Values in mA. PSI=0 → ~1069 mA; PSI=100 → ~98 mA.

name: <module>.ShiftTimeEngine
strings:
Desired Shift Time tables for 4-spd transmissions.
    Output: 2D list [3 shifts][17 torque cols] -> seconds.

name: <module>.TCCDutyEngine
strings:
Generate TCC DC Maximum table.
    Output: 2D list [5 temp rows][17 line PSI cols] -> % duty cycle.

name: <module>.TCCDutyEngine.max_duty_cycle
strings:
Default template — values cluster at 95-97% per GM stock.
        Slight curvature: lower at very low line pressure (low cooler flow),
        slight dip mid-pressure at hot ATF (cooler limited).

name: <module>.TransStudio._build_left_panel
strings:
Tabbed settings panel — fixes vertical-cramped layout.
        Tab 1: Basics — Transmission + Drivetrain (most-changed)
        Tab 2: Engine & Converter — Engine RPM + Torque Converter
        Tab 3: Shift Curve — TPS Slope + Spreads + WOT Lead
        Calculate / Export buttons live below the tabs (always visible).
GM transmission family (1996-current). Selecting a model loads its forward gear ratios and sets RWD/FWD-appropriate defaults.
Quick-select common drag/street/truck tire sizes. Selecting one auto-fills the Tire Dia (in) field. Pick '(Custom)' to enter manually.

Loaded tire diameter in inches (NOT sidewall spec — measure or use tire-size calculator). Affects every speed calculation. 275/55R20 ≈ 31.9″, 33×12.5R17 ≈ 33.0″, 26×11×14 slick ≈ 26.0″.

HPT table: General → Speedometer → Tire Revolutions / Mile (Gen III/IV)
          General → Speedometer → Tire Size (Gen V LT)

Rear axle (or front, for FWD) final drive ratio. Tag on the housing or check VIN. Common GM: 3.08, 3.23, 3.42, 3.73, 4.10.

HPT table: General → Speedometer → Final Drive Ratio (all gens)
Also flows into TCM's gear-ratio detection (P0730 windows)
Transfer case / chain reduction. 1.00 for 2WD or 4x4 in HI range. Use the LO-range ratio for off-road tunes (e.g. NP246 LO = 2.72).
Vehicle curb weight in lb. Used only in Time-mode WOT lead to compute acceleration rate per gear. Doesn't matter in RPM mode.
Estimated rear-wheel HP (dyno or dyno-jet calculator). Used only in Time-mode lead. Crank HP * 0.85 is a reasonable estimate if no dyno.

VSS pulses per output-shaft revolution as configured in the PCM. Used to compute speedometer calibration in the Export dialog. Typical GM: 40 (most RWD), 16 (some FWD).

HPT table: General → Speedometer → VSS Count (Gen III/IV)
           General → Speedometer → Pulses Per Mile (computed)
Configure extra shift table modes (Performance/Hot/Cruise for 4-spd, Pattern A/B/Hot for 6+ spd). Pick a Racing/Towing/Eco intent or override fields manually. Also accessible from Tools menu.

Shudder originates in the partial-lockup zone (30-60 MPH, light
throttle, ~1200-2000 RPM) where TCC engages with too little
pressure — clutch material slip-sticks producing harmonic
vibration. Each level raises minimum apply pressure and
restricts lockup to conditions where partial slip can't develop.

Eliminates 6L80 TCC harmonic shudder by restricting partial
lockup. Applies to the TCC Apply Pressure Ramp + min TCC RPM
+ accel lock gear on next Calculate (F5).
Mild  —  65 PSI plateau, +200 RPM min TCC
Moderate  —  90 PSI plateau, +400 RPM min TCC, +1 lock gear
Aggressive  —  full lock (110 PSI), restrict to cruise+WOT only
Hot-engine idle RPM. Used to compute min-speed-per-gear (MinSpeed = idle + 400 RPM). Default 650 fits most LS/LT engines.

Target engine RPM at the 100% TPS upshift point. Set below redline to leave headroom for shift inertia. LS1=6200, LS3=6600, LT1=6500, ZR1/ZL1=6500, stock truck=5800, diesel=3200.

HPT table: Transmission → Auto Shift Properties → WOT RPM (per shift)
           Or: Transmission → General → Maximum Engine Speed

Maximum allowable engine RPM at any WOT downshift. Caps the downshift speed so a 3-2 kickdown doesn't overrev. Set 1500-2000 below shift_rpm so post-downshift RPM stays under redline.

HPT table: Transmission → Auto Shift Properties → Max Downshift RPM

Minimum engine RPM at which TCC is allowed to lock per gear. Becomes a per-gear MPH floor in the TCC tables. Stock GM ~1100-1200, performance ~1400, towing ~1600 (more slip for torque multiplication).

HPT table: Transmission → Torque Converter → Minimum Lock RPM
           Indirectly: TCC Lock vs TPS (per gear)

Torque converter stall speed (foot-braked, WOT). Drives the slip model: slip% = (stall/1000)^1.7. Stock LS1=1800-2000, mild performance=2400-2800, race=3200+.

HPT informational only — no PCM table directly stores stall RPM.
Affects: TCC Apply Pressure schedules + WOT shift point lead math.

OPTIONAL: dyno-measured WOT slip % at the stall RPM (engine RPM minus driveshaft RPM, divided by engine RPM × 100). Leave at 0.0 to skip. When set, the validation banner will compare your measured slip vs the formula prediction and warn if stall RPM looks wrong.

Lowest gear that TCC is allowed to lock in. Gears BELOW this are forced to 255 MPH (disabled sentinel). Setting higher than the top gear disables lockup completely. Default 2 (gear 1 unlocked). Raising this will auto-raise Accel and WOT Gear to match.

Lowest gear where TCC engages aggressively under acceleration. At/above this gear, lock is pulled close to the upshift speed. Performance tune: 2-3. Tow tune: 4+ (lets converter multiply torque). Cannot be lower than Min Gear (auto-enforced).

Lowest gear that locks TCC through a WOT shift. The 100% TPS cell of lock is pulled up to upshift_OUT - spread. Top gear uses upshift_INTO + spread (locks right after the shift). Typical: 6L80=5, 8L90=7, 10L80=8. Cannot be lower than Min Gear (auto-enforced).
Open advanced TCC behavior flags (stall lock logic, init lock, etc.)
Per-gear WOT shift RPM. Override the global WOT Shift RPM to keep the engine in its powerband across the gear stack (e.g. 6500 in 1-2 for full power, 6100 in 5-6 for cruise).
Edit each gear's WOT upshift RPM. Values feed into the calc as per-gear overrides. Click 'Reset to Global' to revert to the WOT Shift RPM spinbox value.
Set all per-shift values to match the WOT Shift RPM spinbox. Clears per-shift customization (per_gear_rpm = None).

Start at the global WOT Shift RPM for 1→2, then drop 200 RPM
per subsequent shift. Common pattern for boosted builds: full
power on launch, taper for cruise gears (e.g. 6800/6600/6400…).

If a torque curve is loaded, set each shift RPM such that the
engine lands in its peak-HP band after the shift. Picks the
RPM that maximizes the next gear's avg HP across its band.
Falls back to the global RPM if no curve is loaded.

Modify engine torque/HP at WOT for turbo or supercharged setups.
Multiplier: effective_tq = base_tq * (1 + boost_psi * pct/100)
Typical: turbo 7-9% per PSI, supercharger 5-6% per PSI.

Toggle whether boost contributes to torque/HP at runtime.
OFF = naturally aspirated (no scaling).
ON = base curve × boost multiplier per RPM.

RPM at which boost begins to rise meaningfully (above turbo lag).
Typical: small turbo ~2000-2500, large single ~3000-3800.

Peak boost in PSI. Set 0 to disable boost contribution.
Typical: stock turbo 6-10 PSI, mid build 12-18 PSI, race 20+ PSI.

RPM at which peak boost is achieved.
Typical: small turbo ~3500-4500, supercharger nearly immediate.

Boost PSI at redline. Equal to Peak PSI = flat shelf (stock).
Less than Peak PSI = boost taper (common on small turbos or for
exhaust-heat / wastegate creep reasons). Greater = unlikely.

% torque gain per PSI of boost. Empirical multiplier — varies
by engine, ICAT, fuel, octane:
  Turbo, intercooled, pump 91: ~7-8% per PSI
  Turbo, race fuel/E85:        ~8-9% per PSI
  Supercharger, intercooled:   ~5-6% per PSI (parasitic loss)

Throttle body / pedal-mapping preset. Overwrites the 4 sliders below. ETC offsets are positive because drive-by-wire blades don't open until ~8-15% pedal. Cable TBs are 1:1 (offset 0). 'Custom' = no-op.
Pedal % at which the slope curve starts rising (compensates for ETC dead zone). 0 = curve starts at 0% pedal (cable TBs). Higher = curve shifted right (ETC). Negative = aggressive low-TPS shifts.
Exponent of the TPS slope curve: (TPS/100)^factor. 1.0 = linear. >1 = held longer at low throttle, climbs sharper near WOT. <1 = early upshifts, lazy WOT. Default 1.35 fits stock LS tuning.
Upshift firmness 0-10. Blends an aggressive curve into the base. 0 = mushy / late shifts. 10 = quick, firm WOT shifts. Performance: 7-10. Tow/economy: 3-5.

Downshift firmness 0-10. Controls kickdown aggressiveness.
  • HIGHER (7-10): downshift triggers at HIGHER speed — pressing
    throttle drops a gear readily even at cruise speed (snappy
    kickdown for racing/towing/spirited driving)
  • LOWER (1-4):   downshift only at LOWER speed — engine has to
    lug down before PCM drops a gear (eco / hunt-free cruise)
  • 5 = balanced default
Tip: if Normal feels lazy on throttle pickup, bump this to 7-8.
Minimum MPH gap between upshift and downshift in a given gear. Prevents shift hunting. Default 4.5. Higher for tight ratios (8L90/10L80: 5-6), lower for wide ratios (4L60E: 3-4).

Minimum MPH gap between TCC Lock and Unlock (hysteresis).
Stops the converter from oscillating around the lock point.
Stock GM uses 2-3 — TOO TIGHT for worn fluid or aftermarket
converters; expect lock/unlock hunting. Recommended:
  4-5 MPH: street build, fresh fluid
  5-7 MPH: high-mile build or aftermarket converter
  7-8 MPH: race converter with low stall
Minimum MPH gap between Upshift and TCC Lock. Ensures TCC locks BEFORE the upshift fires. Too tight = lock and shift overlap (rough feel). Default 3.0.
Minimum MPH gap between TCC Unlock and the downshift speed. Stops you from unlocking and immediately downshifting. Default 3.5. Increase to 4-5 for smoother cruise.
Geometric lead — early shift derived from gear ratio. Higher ratio = more inertia = more lead. Ignores Weight/RWHP.
Physics-based lead — accel rate = RWHP*0.75*375 / V / Weight (MPH/s). Uses per-gear shift delays (Tools > Edit Shift Delays). More accurate but requires accurate weight + RWHP inputs.
RPM-mode lead magnitude (1-8). Higher = shift earlier. 6L80: 2.5, 8L90: 2.0, 10L80: 1.5 (tighter ratios need less lead). Time-mode ignores this — uses per-gear delay table instead.
Total downshift response time (seconds) — sum of command delay and clutch fill time. Stock GM: 0.30-0.50. Aftermarket valve body: 0.15-0.25. Used in Time-mode lead only.

name: <module>.TransStudio._apply_safety_overlay
strings:
Color-code cells that violate physical / logical constraints.
        Errors (red bg): hard violations that would cause a CEL or bad shift.
        Warnings (orange bg): suspect values that may be intentional.

        Rules (refined to avoid false positives at low TPS):
          - Downshift > Upshift - spread_up  → ERROR (illegal hysteresis)
          - TCC Lock < TCC Unlock + spread   → ERROR (no hysteresis margin)
          - Cell > 200 MPH                   → WARN (probably wrong tire/axle/ratio)
          - Cell < 0                         → ERROR (negative speed)

        Removed (caused false positives at low TPS):
          - "Downshift within 1 MPH of upshift floor" — at TPS 0% the natural
            curve shape compresses the gap to exactly spread_up, which is the
            ENFORCED minimum, not a hunting risk.
          - "Lock > Upshift OUT speed" — at low TPS this is intentional (don't
            lock in this gear, upshift first). At WOT in top gears it's also
            intentional (unlock before shift, relock after).
MPH is very high — verify tire/axle/ratio

name: <module>.TransStudio._build_pdf_report
